dedupe_keys.name: incidenthub h1 2026 cloud and saas reliability report 30 246 outages across 1 082 providers

description: This IncidentHub report analyses outages reported on public provider status pages in the first half of 2026: 30,246 outages across 1,082 providers, with May the busiest month at 6,070 incidents, cloud providers leading with 4,723 outages and developer tools next with 4,589. It breaks the period down by layer, cloud providers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle), edge, CDN and DNS (Cloudflare, Fastly, Akamai), identity and access management, developer tools, collaboration, AI and LLM services, payments, observability and education platforms, and discusses cascade patterns such as LLM outages disrupting downstream tools and IAM as a login bottleneck. Producer: IncidentHub, an outage monitoring service; an outage starts when a provider's status page reports degraded performance or an issue and closes when marked resolved, with durations from the first acknowledgment to resolution in UTC and maintenance excluded. Coverage: 1,082 providers with continuous monitoring from 1 January to 30 June 2026. Access: a free public web report; no downloadable dataset was found on the page. Licence and cost: not stated; free. Caveats: status pages usually reflect outages that affect many customers, provider-reported resolution may lag real restoration, and smaller outages are missed. Simulation uses: the counts and cascade patterns give event data for resilience and cascading-failure studies of cloud dependencies. Related records: the Axis cloud outage tracker (data-axis-cloud-outage-tracker-2026) and the Uptime Institute annual outage analysis (data-uptime-annual-outage-analysis).
